Name: Jeet
ReviewText: We stayed at Padma Homestay at Dhotrey while planning our Tonglu trek. Initially we had booked the place for just one night, but by the time we were supposed to leave, none of us really wanted to go.  We reached around 5 PM in the rain, completely unprepared for the cold especially me, standing there in a T-shirt and shorts and literally shivering! But the moment we stepped inside, their warmth and hospitality made us forget the weather outside. They served us steaming hot rice with delicious Bengali homemade dishes, and after a long journey, that meal felt like absolute heaven.  The rooms were cosy, the atmosphere was peaceful, and the hospitality was genuinely heartfelt. But what made our stay truly special was Padma Didi and her family. She has the sweetest little six year young daughter, Rinchen and as luck would have it, her birthday was on September 5th. So, instead of leaving, we extended our stay and got to be part of their little home celebration.  And honestly it didn't feel like we were guests at a homestay anymore it felt like we were celebrating in our own home. We danced, sang, ate wonderful homemade food, laughed endlessly and had an absolute banger of a night.  A very special mention to our group's little bundle of energy Chini, who made sure absolutely nobody was sitting quietly and had everyone dancing their hearts out!  There are certain trips you remember for the places you visit, and then there are trips you remember for the people you meet. Our two days at Padma Homestay belong firmly to the second category. For those two days, we never once felt away from home. Padma Didi and her family welcomed us with so much warmth, affection and generosity that leaving actually felt a little difficult.  Highly recommended for anyone looking for a cosy, authentic and genuinely homely stay at Dhotrey. Name: Doli Mallick
ReviewText: Recently, we stayed for two days at Padma Homestay. We were in Room No. 10 (view room) of the new building. The room was quite nice and clean, and the bathroom was also clean. Hot water was available all the time. The dining area is downstairs, and the food was quite good and tasty.  The homestay is run by Padma Di, her brother-in-law, and his wife. All of them are very cooperative and helpful. Since it’s very cold there, they always provided both hot and cold drinking water whenever needed.  We were lucky to see Kanchenjunga on both days. It is visible from our room, and the view is even better from the rooftop.  Dhotrey itself is a very beautiful place. We explored the surrounding areas on foot. A short walk away, there is a Shiva temple, a monastery, and a viewpoint. Another road leads towards Sandakphu.  In the evening, Padma herself does karaoke 🤓. It’s quite enjoyable to listen to—gives a bit of a Goa vibe in the mountains! However, some people might feel it disturbs their sleep at night. Name: niladdit saha
ReviewText: Padma Homestay probably is the best place to stay at Dhotrey.  I've seen negative reviews about this place and have wondered how low the concept of trekking has gone down to. This is a homestay, which is supposed to give you a chance to live WITH them, they are not supposed to host you like a hotel.  Nice, modest, clean rooms with adequate blankets provided. Fully functional toilets with faucets and flush operational, unless temperature dips below freezing point.  Geysers available. All around balcony provides marvellous views. Top floor rooms have a dedicated dining space.  Common dining space is at the lowest floor with heating arrangement. Seating arrangements on floor. Delicious meals (full course meals, that are usually rare on trek routes) with amazing hospitality. Hot water and black tea is available all the time, just ask them.  Tip: Homestays are best enjoyed if you talk to people. Talk to the owners, talk to other guests, share stories and food supplies, stay at the dining space most of the time. Don't expect hotel amenities and don't expect Kanchenjunga all the time, you get those if you're fortunate!
